inputSentence: Eurovision Song Contest 2025 is being held in Basel from May 13 to May 17.
heroSummary: Eurovision is part live music competition, part continental political weather vane, and part internet event. Basel's edition needs a page that can hold schedule details, country narratives, fan momentum, and the finalists' changing odds in one place.
whatChanged: Once host city, semi-final dates, and production details are locked, Eurovision stops being a long-range calendar note and becomes a live, update-heavy cultural event.
whyItMatters: Eurovision reliably spills past entertainment coverage into identity, diplomacy, meme culture, and the business of staging one of Europe's biggest annual broadcasts.

timeline.title: Switzerland wins the previous contest
timeline.description: Nemo's victory sends hosting rights to Switzerland and starts the race to define the next edition's city, venue, and production tone.

timeline.title: Basel is selected as host
timeline.description: The host-city choice shifts coverage toward venue logistics, local economic impact, and how the city intends to stage an event built for both TV and fan tourism.

timeline.title: Contest week unfolds live
timeline.description: The story turns into a rapid stream of qualifier results, staging surprises, jury-versus-televote tension, and the cultural conversation around standout acts.

watchItems.title: Semi-final qualifiers
watchItems.description: The shape of the grand final changes quickly once fan favorites either survive or fall out in the semi-finals.

watchItems.title: Staging breakthroughs
watchItems.description: Eurovision coverage often pivots on performance design, camera language, and whether a live concept lands more powerfully than the studio track.

watchItems.title: National narratives
watchItems.description: Every finalist arrives with a domestic media frame, and those narratives often influence how international audiences read the performances.

watchItems.title: Voting drama
watchItems.description: The final scoreboard story is not only who wins, but whether juries and televoters reward the same kinds of entries.

entities.name: European Broadcasting Union
entities.detail: Sets the contest rules, coordinates participating broadcasters, and controls the official event schedule and production framework.

entities.name: Basel
entities.detail: Becomes a protagonist in its own right through venue logistics, fan zones, hospitality demand, and civic branding.

entities.name: Participating broadcasters
entities.detail: Each broadcaster shapes the pipeline from domestic selection to the final televised performance seen across Europe and beyond.

coverageAngles.title: The contest as a live internet event
coverageAngles.description: Beyond the TV audience, Eurovision is a social-media-native spectacle whose most important reactions often happen in real time online.

coverageAngles.title: How host cities use Eurovision
coverageAngles.description: Track how Basel converts a global broadcast into a tourism and place-branding opportunity.

coverageAngles.title: Performance concept versus song strength
coverageAngles.description: A recurring editorial question is whether staging can elevate a middling song or expose a weak live act.

coverageAngles.title: Identity and geopolitics on stage
coverageAngles.description: Eurovision often doubles as a soft-power venue where symbolism, language choice, and representation matter nearly as much as the music itself.

faq.question: Why does Eurovision need a bespoke page shape?
faq.answer: Because the audience wants a mix of logistics, entertainment analysis, live results, and fan-culture context rather than a generic event brief.

faq.question: What changes from semi-finals to final?
faq.answer: The emphasis shifts from discovery and elimination to ranking outcomes, vote splits, and the winner's immediate cultural afterlife.

faq.question: What would editors likely update most often?
faq.answer: Qualifiers, running order, standout performances, controversies, and anything that changes the odds heading into the grand final.
